title: Planting a shop that looks lived in
target: How to use the plants in a TCG Card Shop Simulator shop, given that they are placed objects, that pots come in a numbered set with their own levels of detail, and that beds and trees are separate pieces.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: Room in the shop you are not using for stock
A little money set aside for decoration
An idea of which corner you want to soften

steps.do: Buy a plant as an object to place rather than as a finish to paint on.
steps.because: the game names a set of plants you can interact with and place (Interactable_Plant1, Interactable_Plant2, Interactable_Plant8)

steps.do: Pick a pot from the numbered set and leave it where people will stand near it.
steps.because: the pots are a numbered set, several of them with more than one level of detail (Flower_Pot_01, Flower_Pot_02_LOD0, Flower_Pot_08_LOD1)

steps.do: Use a bed for a low run along a wall rather than lining up pots.
steps.because: flower beds are named as their own pieces, separate from the pots (Flowerbed01, Flowerbed03, Flowerbed06)

steps.do: Spend the tree on one corner rather than repeating it round the room.
steps.because: trees are named in kinds, a muffin tree and two evolution trees among them (TreeA, MuffinTreeA, StarfishEvoTree_Mesh, PiggyEvoTree_Mesh)

steps.do: Do not be surprised to meet the same tree again in another palette.
steps.because: there are ghost versions of a tree and of a flower (Ghost_TreeD, Ghost_FlowerD)

commonMistakes: Buying a pot and expecting a bed, when the two are separate pieces.
Filling the busiest corner with a tree and leaving customers nowhere to stand.
Repeating one plant round the whole room so the shop looks like a showroom.
Treating the planting as free: it is bought and placed like anything else.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
